A United ISD trustee walked out of a board workshop early this week — to attend a candidate forum for a different school district. And a fellow trustee called her out for it, publicly, before walking it back.

According to the Laredo Morning Times, UISD trustee Michelle Molina, who is running for reelection, left a UISD board workshop early to attend an LISD candidate forum organized by MOVE Texas, STX Frontera, CMPSCHL Creative and the Carnalismo Brown Berets. Fellow trustee Dianelle Martinez criticized the move in a social media post — then retracted the criticism.

What she missed

The workshop wasn't filler. Among the items on the table: 16 special-education aide vacancies in the district — part of the staffing shortage United ISD has been wrestling with for weeks, the same shortage the district has tried to fill with incentive bonuses and a special-education job fair.

Molina cited a child's birthday and prior meetings as her reasons for leaving early.

Why it matters

Board workshops are where the unglamorous work gets done — staffing gaps, budgets, the machinery of a district that serves tens of thousands of students. When a sitting trustee, mid-reelection campaign, leaves that work early to appear at another district's candidate forum, voters get to ask a fair question: who is the time being spent on?

Martinez's criticism — and her retraction — says something too: that even inside the board, the optics looked bad enough to spark a public fight, and politically hot enough to make a trustee back down.

Election Day is November 3. Early voting is underway. UISD voters will decide whether Molina's record — workshops included — earns another term.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times — “UISD trustee criticized after leaving board workshop for LISD candidate forum” (Oct. 22, 2026)

title: UISD trustee Molina leaves board workshop early for rival district's forum — colleague cries foul, then backs down
